commit_message:
[revec][wasm][turboshaft] Support intersecting ForcePackNode

The force-packed nodes are inconsecutive values by nature, which may
induce intersecting PackNode. The current node_to_packnode map can only
support 1:1 mapping that does not allow overlapped PackNode.

This patch adds new structures to store the intersected PackNodes and
make them mergable from other trees or branches in the same tree.
It also adds support of force-packing ReplaceLane operations which
is commonly accompanied by intersecting PackNodes in real-life cases.

findings.title: Incomplete dependency check allows unsafe force-packing of interdependent nodes
findings.message: SLPTree::HasInputDependencies performs a BFS to verify that two nodes can safely be force-packed together (i.e., neither depends on the other). However, it has two critical omissions. First, it does not track 'reorder inputs': when a node has already been identified as an intermediate node in the BFS of a prior force-pack dependency check (across SLPTrees), that node may later itself be nominated for force-packing, breaking the assumption that nodes with smaller OpIndex will always be emitted before nodes with larger OpIndex. The commit introducing intersecting ForcePackNode created exactly this scenario, where a force-packing node from one SLPTree becomes an input of a force-packing node in another SLPTree that gets reduced earlier. Second, the BFS traversal does not check for side effects between intermediate nodes: even without a direct data-dependency path, if there are side-effecting operations between the BFS boundary and the candidate start node, reordering is unsafe. These two omissions cause NewForcePackNode and NewIntersectPackNode to create invalid force-pack pairings. At reduction time, ReduceForceOrIntersectPackNode then tries to emit out-of-order inputs using ReduceInputsOfOp, operating on nodes whose output mappings are not yet established, ultimately leading to a segfault in the generated JSToWasm wrapper trampoline.
findings.suggestion: Before the BFS, check whether either node in the group is already a tracked 'reorder input' (i.e., it appeared as an intermediate node during a prior HasInputDependencies call from a different SLPTree context). If so, return true immediately to reject the force-pack. Additionally, during the BFS, for each intermediate input between start and end, verify IsSideEffectFree(start_prev, input) — if any side effects exist, return true. After a successful BFS (returning false), merge all traversed intermediate nodes into the reorder_inputs_ set so they are excluded from future force-packing attempts.

ground_truth.root_cause: SLPTree::HasInputDependencies incorrectly returns false (no dependency) in two scenarios: (1) when either candidate node is already a 'reorder input' from a prior cross-SLPTree traversal — the function does not track such nodes; and (2) when side-effecting operations exist between intermediate BFS nodes and the start node — the function omits an IsSideEffectFree check. Both gaps allow NewForcePackNode and NewIntersectPackNode to create logically invalid pairings, leading to incorrect code generation and a crash.
